Name: ZuzuMarket
Author: Flenuc
Description:
[size=5][b]Description[/b][/size]
[b]Zuzu Stock Exchange[/b] turns Pelican Town into a living economy inspired by Argentina. Prices react to what you sell, inflation raises costs every day, the tax office sends you bills, and Valle Inversiones opens the doors of a full stock exchange: stocks, bonds, futures, options... and, if things go wrong, attachments and bankruptcy.

Grow from a small [i]monotributista[/i] farmer into the owner of a listed corporation, hedge your harvest with futures, save in Gotoro gold to beat inflation and make friends with Julián Ferreyra, your stockbroker. Every coin you earn or spend goes through real double-entry books.

[i]Español:[/i] la [b]Bolsa de Valores de Zuzu[/b] convierte Pueblo Pelícano en una economía viva al estilo argentino: precios que reaccionan a tus ventas, inflación, impuestos, una bolsa completa, tus propias empresas, deudas con consecuencias y el oro gotoro con cepo y blue.

[size=5][b]Installation instructions[/b][/size]
[list=1]
[*]Install the latest version of [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/2400]SMAPI[/url].[/*]
[*]Download this mod and unzip it into your [font=Courier New]Stardew Valley/Mods[/font] folder (you should end up with [font=Courier New]Mods/ZuzuMarket[/font]).[/*]
[*](Optional) Install [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu[/url] to change the settings in game.[/*]
[*]Run the game through SMAPI and load a save. The economy starts that day: new or existing saves both work.[/*]
[*]Choose your difficulty ([i]casual[/i], [i]realista[/i] or [i]argentina[/i]) [b]before[/b] loading the save: each save keeps the difficulty it started with.[/*]
[/list][b]Getting started:[/b] find the Valle Inversiones phone next to the town board, or the Stock Agency, and open the Terminal. Open your brokerage account to get the recipe for a Terminal you can craft for your farm. Pay your tax bills each season at Mayor Lewis's town ledger, at the Agency or with auto debit.

[b]Uninstalling:[/b] remove any Terminal you crafted on your farm first; then delete the [font=Courier New]ZuzuMarket[/font] folder. Your gold, items and buildings stay as they are.

[size=5][b]Main features[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]Commodities with supply and demand[/b] — 15 products (wheat, corn, parsnip, pumpkin, milk, eggs, copper, iron, gold, fish, wine and more). Sell too much and the price sinks; seasons, weather, events and news move the market.[/*]
[*][b]Inflation[/b] — a daily price index that affects shops, Robin's buildings, taxes and bonds.[/*]
[*][b]Argentine-style taxes[/b] — Monotributo, then VAT-registered business: IVA, gross income tax, municipal fees, property fees and income tax with advances. Late payments bring interest, formal notices and collections.[/*]
[*][b]Stock exchange (BYMZ)[/b] — 10 fictional companies with charts and dividends, the MERZU index, Treasury bills, repos, sovereign and corporate bonds (fixed, floating and inflation-linked), credit ratings, defaults and restructurings, and a central bank that sets the policy rate.[/*]
[*][b]Derivatives (MATZU)[/b] — commodity futures with daily margin and [b]physical delivery[/b] from your Storage Silo, and stock options.[/*]
[*][b]Debts with consequences[/b] — attachments, insolvency proceedings and bankruptcy (in Argentina mode, optionally losing buildings), bank loans, repo borrowing and your own credit rating.[/*]
[*][b]Your own companies[/b] — Farming, Mining, Fishing, Industrial and Trading companies (LLC or corporation) with their own books and taxes. Export to the Gotoro Empire, issue your own bonds and [b]take your corporation public with an IPO[/b].[/*]
[*][b]The Stock Agency and Julián Ferreyra[/b] — a new building in town and a new NPC with a schedule, market-aware dialogue, gift tastes, three heart events and lower fees as your friendship grows.[/*]
[*][b]Gotoro gold[/b] — a foreign currency with its own exchange rate. In Argentina mode: currency controls with a quota, the MEP dollar through bonds, a black market at Krobus's (beware of raids) and devaluations.[/*]
[*][b]Three difficulty levels[/b] — Casual, Realista and Argentina, measured with year-long simulations.[/*]
[*][b]English and Spanish[/b], Generic Mod Config Menu support and console commands ([font=Courier New]zuzu_*[/font]) to inspect everything.[/*]
[/list]
[size=5][b]Requirements[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Stardew Valley [b]1.6.15[/b] or later (PC).[/*]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/2400]SMAPI[/url] [b]4.0[/b] or later.[/*]
[*]Optional: [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu[/url].[/*]
[*][b]Single player only.[/b] In multiplayer only the host runs the economy.[/*]
[*][b]Compatible with Stardew Valley Expanded[/b]: the mod never replaces maps; the Agency is placed on a free spot of the town and the phone moves to the nearest free tile. Use [font=Courier New]zuzu_compat[/font] to check and [font=Courier New]zuzu_agency here[/font] to move the Agency.[/*]
[*]Other mods that change sell prices may stack with or override market prices.[/*]
[/list]
